page: Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-intel is an instance in the High Performance family built on the x86_64 Intel Xeon platform. The server provisions 12 shared vCPUs across 6 physical cores operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with hyperthreading enabled. It includes 32 KB L1d cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, along with hardware support for AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES cryptography, and BMI2 instructions. System memory totals 24.0 GB, resulting in an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is provided through a bundled 500 GB NVMe SSD. The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and features zero hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent mid-tier multi-threaded compute and data handling capabilities. The server recorded 17,309.27 on stress-ng multi-core and 17,934.88 on PassMark CPU tests, both aligning with the middle 50% band. Uncached memory read bandwidth achieved 87.74 GB/sec and write bandwidth reached 47.62 GB/sec. Redis SET benchmarks yielded 18.53 million operations per second, while static web serving reached 11.99 GB/sec. However, single-thread throughput exhibits lower relative output, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1036.0 in the bottom quartile. Similarly, medium 7B model LLM inference generated 7.43 tokens per second, indicating hardware constraints for complex machine learning tasks.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio paired with integrated NVMe storage yields balanced compute density at a cost profile typical of shared-resource cloud infrastructure. The primary engineering tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and modest 2.0 GHz clock, which restricts performance on latency-sensitive single-threaded tasks. This configuration is well matched for parallelized software builds, static web servers, distributed Redis caching tiers, CI/CD runners, and batch ETL data processing.
